conventions.convention: Hellinger distance uses root-L2 normalization: h²(P,Q)=∫(√p−√q)² dμ, with a fixed dominating measure and supplied density versions.
Density L1 is the full integral ∫|p−q| dμ; event-supremum total variation equals half that integral.

Local prior mass controls directional KL(P0‖Pθ) and P0[log(pθ/p0)]² simultaneously. Weighted log terms are zero where p0=0; where p0>0 and pθ=0, the log ratio is −∞ and its square is +∞. AC is assumed for the imported KL convention.

Packing uses finite subsets with pairwise distances strictly greater than the radius. The entropy, separation, and conclusion use the same selected metric. Density L2 requires one finite almost-everywhere bound for every model density and the truth.

The density family is supplied jointly measurably; parameter sieves are measurable and nonempty. Posterior normalization uses finite positive evidence. Contraction is in sampling probability for sufficiently large fixed M, without an almost-sure or minimax conclusion.
The Hölder example assumes its Hellinger entropy bound and its local KL/log-square prior-mass bound; it does not prove either premise from Hölder regularity alone.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated jointly measurable dominated IID model, choose d to be root-L2 Hellinger, full density L1, or density L2 with a common finite density bound. Suppose εn→0, nεn²→∞, log D(εn,Fn,d)≤nεn², Π(Θnᶜ)≤exp(−(C+4)nεn²), and prior mass at least exp(−Cnεn²) where both KL(P0‖Pθ) and P0[log(pθ/p0)]² are at most εn². Then for all sufficiently large fixed M, Π{θ:d(pθ,p0)>Mεn | X1,…,Xn}→0 in P0ⁿ-probability.

Under the stated same-metric packing condition log D(εn,Fn,d)≤nεn², εn→0 and nεn²→∞, for every fixed M≥128 and all sufficiently large n there is a measurable binary test with null error at most 2exp(−(cdM²−1)nεn²) and error at most exp(−cdM²nεn²) under every p∈Fn satisfying d(p,p0)>Mεn. The constant cd>0 depends only on the selected metric and, for density L2, its common density bound.

For the stated jointly measurable dominated IID model, if Π(Kn)≥exp(−Cnεn²), where Kn controls directional KL and the log-square moment by εn², then the likelihood-ratio denominator Dn is finite and positive P0ⁿ-almost surely and P0ⁿ{Dn≥exp(−(C+2)nεn²)}≥1−1/(nεn²).
For probability densities relative to one fixed measure, h is a metric on the induced probability laws and h(P,Q)²≤d1(P,Q)=2‖P−Q‖TV, while d1(P,Q)≤2h(P,Q).

For independent centered real variables Zi with |Zi|≤b almost surely, b>0, and V=ΣE[Zi²]>0, each one-sided tail of ΣZi at t>0 is bounded by exp(−t²/[2(V+bt/3)]). If V=0, the sum is zero almost surely.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite page uses the same root-L2 Hellinger and event-supremum TV conventions. Batch 11 proves its denominator, tests, and probability contraction locally; it does not import the earlier almost-sure consistency conclusion.

This is a contextual page prerequisite. Its listed items do not cite batch-11 items; the page develops separate likelihood-tilt denominator and testing arguments rather than applying the well-specified contraction theorem to unnormalized tilts.

The main theorem faithfully states and applies the IID denominator and same-metric testing lemmas, enlarging radii to absorb entropy constants. Binary-regression densities are bounded by one for density-L2 testing. Fixed-design regression uses separate non-IID suppliers; expectation convergence is derived from bounded posterior tails converging in probability.

The countable-sieve lemma and mixture results preserve root-L2 normalization and the denominator exponent C+2; prior mass exp(−nδ²) yields exp(−3nδ²). Weighted countable-sieve testing is established separately rather than attributed to the global-entropy theorem.

The type-S weak-BvM theorem cites the bounded-variance Bernstein lemma for empirical wavelet coefficients. Its IID centered bounded summands and finite variance bounds support the stated two-sided Bernstein estimate.
